verdict.line: You lose if you let Nasus freeze the wave and farm Siphoning Strike stacks uncontested past level 6; you win if you deny his CS and force all-ins while W (Path Maker) and your Q poke are still ahead of his stacks.

brief.thesis: Nasus's entire kit is built around uninterrupted Siphoning Strike (Q) last hits and Spirit Fire (E) zone control, and he has no dash or gap-closer to stop you from denying either. K'Sante's 3.5s Q (Ntofo Strikes) cooldown lets him poke on every exchange and his W (Path Maker) comes online at level 3 with a hard stun, so the lane is decided by whether you zone him off cannon waves before his Q damage compounds. The measured 53.4% win rate over 116 games and K'Sante's lane and solo-kill edge confirm this is yours to press, not a lane to sit back in.

theirWindow.when: Spirit Fire (E) zone is live under you
theirWindow.what: Standing in Spirit Fire's armor-shred flame while he trades autos lets his Q damage and Soul Eater lifesteal snowball. Step out of the flame and make him re-cast it (12s cooldown) before continuing the fight.

yourWindow.when: His Siphoning Strike (Q) is on cooldown
yourWindow.what: At early ranks his Q sits on an 8-6s cooldown with only 255 range, so right after he swings, land free Q (Ntofo Strikes) hits and look for the 2-stack shockwave pull to set up a W (Path Maker) stun.

W online, Nasus has no dash to answer

start.why: Highest measured win rate at this stage (56.8% over 118 games, 86.1% pick) and keeps you sustained through the slow early poke exchanges before W is online.

boots.why: Best-performing boots in this matchup (50.6% over 81 games, 61.4% pick); Nasus's damage is entirely auto-attacks, and Steelcaps directly cuts the sustained AA trades he wants.

core.why: The cooldown and slow proc off Q (Ntofo Strikes) makes it easier to land the 2-stack pull and chain into W before he can disengage.
Grievous Wounds-adjacent omnivamp undercuts his Soul Eater lifesteal race in extended trades.
Stacking resistances scale with the fight the same way his stacked Q does, keeping you ahead of his late-game power spike.

situational.when: he builds into heavy lifesteal and Fury of the Sands sustain to out-heal your trades
he picks up attack speed items and tries to abuse Wither's slow uptime to kite you
you need more raw healing to win the sustained trade race instead of pure resistances
his Q stacks are snowballing fast and you need armor plus antiheal online immediately

runes.keystoneWhy: Procs off every Q (Ntofo Strikes) poke exchange and keeps you healthier than his Soul Eater lifesteal through the early trading phase.

summoners.why: Flash+Teleport is the dominant pick (73.6% pick rate, 55.3% win rate) since Teleport lets you reset onto the wave after all-in windows instead of losing CS to his safe farming.

playing.title: Poke every time he reaches for CS
playing.detail: His Siphoning Strike (Q) is on an 8-4s cooldown and only 255 range; punish each last-hit attempt with your 3.5s-cooldown Q (Ntofo Strikes) since he can't retaliate in time.

playing.title: Bait Spirit Fire, don't stand in it
playing.detail: Spirit Fire (E) is a 650-range, 12s-cooldown zone that shreds your armor while you're in it. Make him commit it on empty space, then re-engage after it's down.

playing.title: All-in once W is online
playing.detail: From level 3, W (Path Maker) charges then knocks back and stuns; use it while he's mid-Q animation near the wave, when he can't disengage.

playing.title: Stack Q to 2 before committing W
playing.detail: Ntofo Strikes grants a stack on hit; at 2 stacks it fires a pulling shockwave. Land that pull first so he can't walk out of W's stun range.

playing.title: Respect Wither before diving
playing.detail: Wither (W, 700 range) decelerates your movement and attack speed, which directly counters Footwork's (E) dash. Bait it out with E's shield-dash before you commit to an extended fight.

playing.title: Stop dueling once he's visibly stacked
playing.detail: His Q damage compounds permanently on kills. Once his stack count is clearly ahead, shift to poke and wave control instead of standing trades.

playing.title: Use R to finish fights, not open them
playing.detail: All Out (R) knocks him through walls and transforms your kit at the cost of reduced defenses; land the wall-slam then burst him down before his Fury of the Sands (120s cooldown) can turn a drawn-out fight.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, runes, summoners, and win-rate figures above are measured from live games on the current patch (16.20.1); the mechanical reasoning and trade-pattern advice are my own tactical read.
